explanation: The highest military leaders or commanders under Roman rule, often mentioned together with religious leaders as opponents of Jesus.
Followers of a strict Jewish sect that placed great emphasis on observing the written and oral law (Torah) and the traditions of the elders.
The name of the royal dynasty in Galilee, here specifically Herod Antipas, who was a tetrarch under Roman rule and a political opponent of Jesus.
A contribution or levy demanded from the population for the Roman state, a topic used in the trap about paying tribute to Caesar.
The Roman ruler (Tiberius), represented by the coin bearing his image and title, a symbol of political power that Jesus was challenged to acknowledge.
The teaching that the dead will be raised at a future time, a central theme in the debate between Jesus and the Sadducees.
A Jewish group consisting of priests who did not believe in the resurrection of the dead or in any spiritual realm beyond the written Torah.
The lineage of Israel's greatest king, used in the debate over whether the Messiah is David's son (according to the flesh) and at the same time his Lord (in a divine sense).
God's chosen messengers who spoke on God's behalf; Jesus uses them to show that Scripture testifies to a unified truth.
The sanctuary in Jerusalem, the center of Jewish worship and sacrifice, where Jesus taught and challenged the authorities.
